name: Iris Pattern Consistency
description: Tracks iris texture pattern consistency over time — AI-generated irises often change pattern across frames.
mechanism:
This method detects deepfakes by analyzing the temporal stability of iris texture patterns, which are unique biometric identifiers that should remain constant across video frames:

1. **Iris Region Segmentation and Normalization**: The method detects the iris region by fitting concentric circles to the pupil boundary (inner) and limbus boundary (outer) using gradient-based circle detection (Daugman, 2004). The annular iris region is unwrapped into a rectangular normalized representation using Daugman's rubber-sheet model — mapping from polar coordinates (r, θ) to a fixed-size rectangle (typically 64×512 pixels). This normalization compensates for pupil dilation, gaze direction, and distance changes, enabling direct comparison of iris texture across frames regardless of eye appearance changes.

2. **IrisCode Feature Extraction**: The normalized iris texture is encoded using 2D Gabor wavelets at multiple frequencies and orientations, producing a binary iris code (Daugman, 2004). Each bit represents the sign of the Gabor filter response at a specific location, frequency, and orientation. The resulting 2048-bit iris code is a compact, rotation-invariant representation of the iris texture. For each frame, the method extracts this code and computes the fractional Hamming distance (HD) between iris codes from consecutive frames. Real irises produce HD < 0.32 between any two captures of the same eye (the Daugman decision boundary). Different irises produce HD ≈ 0.50 (random binary strings).

3. **Temporal Iris Code Stability**: In authentic video, the iris code extracted from consecutive frames of the same eye should be highly consistent — HD < 0.15 between adjacent frames (the variation comes only from noise, eyelid occlusion, and segmentation imprecision). The method computes the iris code for every frame and tracks HD over time. Real eyes show: (a) low baseline HD (< 0.15) during fixation periods, (b) brief HD spikes during blinks (partial iris occlusion), (c) moderate HD increases during large saccades (motion blur). Deepfake eyes show: (a) higher baseline HD (> 0.25) because the generator produces different iris textures per frame, (b) gradual HD drift over time as the generated iris pattern evolves, (c) no correlation between HD spikes and detected blinks.

4. **Bilateral Iris Consistency**: Both eyes of the same person should produce different but individually stable iris codes. The method validates that: (a) left and right iris codes are distinct (HD > 0.40, confirming they are different irises), (b) each eye's iris code is individually temporally stable (HD < 0.15 between frames), (c) the temporal stability of both eyes is correlated — HD spikes should co-occur (during blinks, both eyes close simultaneously). Deepfakes often fail bilateral consistency because each eye may be generated independently, producing correlated temporal instabilities that do not match physiological blink patterns.
parameters:
Iris segmentation: integrodifferential operator (Daugman)
Normalization: rubber-sheet model, 64×512 output
Iris code: 2D Gabor wavelets, 2048 bits
Hamming distance threshold: < 0.32 for identity match
Temporal stability: HD < 0.15 between adjacent frames
Bilateral consistency: HD > 0.40 between left and right eyes
Blink detection: eyelid aperture tracking
Minimum iris diameter: 50 pixels
Frame rate requirement: ≥ 15 fps
Occlusion tolerance: up to 40% iris occlusion by eyelids
accuracy: 83–91% accuracy detecting deepfakes via iris temporal consistency. Temporal iris code stability achieves AUC of 0.88 on FaceForensics++. Bilateral iris consistency provides F1-score of 0.86. Combined analysis achieves AUC of 0.91. Performance requires sufficient eye resolution (≥ 50 pixels iris diameter) and degrades with heavy compression (CRF > 30) and low frame rate.
source: Daugman, J. (2004). How Iris Recognition Works. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology, 14(1), 21–30.
useCase: Detecting face swap deepfakes through iris pattern instability. Biometric liveness verification via iris consistency. Forensic authentication of video testimony. Detecting AI-generated faces in video conferencing scenarios.
strengths:
• Based on established iris biometric technology (Daugman's IrisCode)
• Iris patterns are unique and permanent — strong ground truth
• Temporal stability provides definitive video-specific signal
• Bilateral analysis adds physiological plausibility check
• Works even when other facial regions are manipulated
limitations:
• Requires high-resolution eye images (≥ 50 pixels iris diameter)
• Gaze direction away from camera reduces visible iris area
• Dark irises (brown/black) have lower contrast texture patterns
• Glasses and reflections can obscure iris detail
• Some advanced generators may learn to produce temporally stable synthetic irises
